item.title: Lego Robotics for Elementary Students — Sat Aug 29, 1:00 PM — RecRoom
item.description: LEGO Robotics for Elementary Kids (Grades K–5) LEGO Robotics at Kinetic Minds introduces kids to engineering and beginner coding through hands-on building, testing, and problem-solving using LEGO robotics kits. In this small-group, drop-in friendly workshop, kids work in pairs to build real robots, program simple behaviors, and improve their designs through guided challenges. The focus is on curiosity, experimentation, and learning how things work—there’s no single “right” build and no step-by-step cookie-cutter instructions. Workshops are intentionally capped at a low student-to-instructor ratio to support collaboration, confidence, and meaningful learning. Kids will explore: • Engineering and building with LEGO robotics components • Beginner coding concepts (motors, sensors, cause and effect) • Testing, debugging, and iterating designs • Teamwork, communication, and explaining ideas Details: • 60-minute session • Small-group format • No prior experience required Community Spons

item.title: Tea & Tarot - A Bookclub Style Discussion Group — Thu Sep 17, 7:00 PM — the Space
item.description:
Monthly Gathering | Thursday, September 17th | 7:00 PM – 8:30 PM | The Space | $25 Calling all tarot lovers, both new and seasoned! Join us for an intimate way of exploring the cards. What could be better than a cozy evening of warm tea and deep conversation? Join us for Tea & Tarot with Gina Devine—a monthly, book club-style discussion group created to deepen our connection with the archetypes of the tarot through community and shared insight. Rather than a formal class, this is a casual meet-up where we treat the tarot as a living text. Based on the psychological insights of Carl Jung, we will explore the Major Arcana not just as fortune-telling tools, but as mirrors of our own lives, rituals, and transformations. item.description: Major Kickoff a high-energy, campus-wide event that transforms a traditional majors fair into an interactive and dynamic experience that sets the tone for major exploration. Major Kickoff serves as a central hub where exploratory ("undeclared") students can dive into the wide array of majors offered at Montclair in a fun and engaging way. Students will engage with peers, faculty, and staff; discover pathways to get involved in various programs; and gain the guidance they need to make confident, informed decisions about their major. With the opportunity to declare a major on the spot, Major Kickoff empowers students to take charge of their academic journey. With over 50 departments, programs, clubs, and more on site, you never know what you might discover or who you might meet. Enjoy free food, games, music, and giveaways, win prizes and T-shirts, and maybe even discover your major. item.title: Reimagining the Tarot: An Intuitive Collage Workshop — Sun Sep 27, 12:30 PM
item.description: What if the Tarot could speak in your voice? In this exploratory workshop, we’ll dive into the rich history and symbolism of the Major Arcana — exploring the colors, archetypes, and allegories that have given these iconic cards their power for centuries. Then, we’ll turn that wisdom over to your own creative instincts. No art experience needed. No tarot experience needed. Just an open mind and a willingness to listen to what’s stirring inside you. You’ll choose a card that calls to you, journal your reflections, and then bring it to life through drawing, painting, or collage — reimagining it through your own symbols, style, and personal expression. The goal isn’t perfection; it’s presence. We’re letting intuition lead. 📅 Sunday, September 27 | 12:30 pm – 3:00 pm 📍 The Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Loft #2, Montclair, NJ 🎟 The first 1.5 hours is the lecture about the major arcana and symbolism for $45 Returning participants can choose to skip the lecture and arrive at 2:00 pm for $

item.title: Tech Talks — Thu Oct 15, 3:30 PM — Montclair Main - Classroom
item.description:
Tech Talks is a free informational series where library staff introduce and explain the technology topics that matter most in today's digital world. Each session takes a closer look at a new or complex topic—whether it's a trending app, an emerging technology, or a platform you've been hearing about but aren't quite sure how to navigate. Through demonstrations and clear, jargon-free explanations, you'll come away with a better understanding of the tech landscape around you. There's no hands-on component, so no devices are needed—just come ready to learn and ask questions.
All are welcome regardless of experience level, and time is reserved at the end of each session for Q&A. Sessions are free and open to the public.

item.title: Concert: Marc Berger — Sun Sep 13, 2:00 PM — West Orange - Community Room 1
item.description:
Presentation
RIDE currently offers ten cinematic recordings that capture the grandeur and allure of the West while examining its profound origins in the American psyche. Marc and Mike Ricciardi created the album, which is based on Marc's lifelong love affair with the American West. "Twister" has a melancholy message and beat, "Take It on the Chin" is about taming a wild horse, "Time Waits For No Man" is about a sexy, mind-blowing encounter in the middle of nowhere, and seven more scenic stops make up RIDE's Great American Frontier tour.
About the artist
Marc's life revolves around two passions: composing and performing original songs and touring the American West. At SXSW Music Festival and Kerrville Folk Festival, he has opened for big stars like Bob Dylan and sang his antinuclear hymn "The Last One," a mainstay of Richie Havens' shows.
Source: Libcal Bccls 10341

item.title: Jean Luc Godard's Breathless (1960) French film introduction — Wed Sep 16, 6:30 PM — West Orange - Community Room 1
item.description:
Program
We invite you to join us for this fascinating introduction to the French New Wave, which redefined storytelling in film during the '50s and '60s. The event commences with a perceptive introduction given by Gerard Amsellem, who is an artist, educator, and founder of New Wave Productions and the Institute of Art and Film Studies. It concludes with a showing of Breathless (À bout de souffle), a legendary film by Jean-Luc Godard, which is widely regarded as the film that sparked modern cinema. Stay for an interactive Q&A with Amsellem after the film to discuss the film's unique cutting techniques, the groundbreaking roles played by the performers, and the director's vision.
Artist
Gerard Amsellem is an artist, educator, and filmmaker holding dual citizenship in the U.S. and France. With a background in painting and advanced degrees in French literature and art history from the University of Paris, he later continued his education at New York University's Tisch School of the Arts

item.description:
Program
Before the revolution altered the course of Cuban music, a band of young musicians in Havana in the 1950s had already begun to shake things up. In a surprising twist, the band reunited forty years later to record the songs they had left behind, and the result was the best-selling album in the history of world music. Performers from the 1999 documentary film Son Cubano and the Tony-winning 2025 Broadway musical Buena Vista Social Club are included in the presentation, which also covers life in Cuba in the 1950s before the revolution.
Artist
At the Performing Arts Center at Penn State University, Rick Feingold oversaw the Latin Jazz series. In addition to his extensive travels throughout Cuba, he teaches history at Bergen Community College. Mr. Feingold has a Bachelor of Arts in History from Rutgers University and an MBA from Penn State University.

The Lenore Raphael Trio consists of Lenore on piano, Hilliard Greene on bass, and Kahlil Kwame Bell on drums, creating a world-class ensemble. Their performance will feature jazz classics and selections from the American songbook.
Artist
Lenore Raphael is a jazz pianist, radio personality, Steinway artist, and jazz educator who is widely considered to be among the top pianists working in modern music. Major jazz clubs and festivals have sold out her performances on multiple occasions. New York City's Birdland, The Blue Note, and Jazz at Lincoln Center were all stops for Dizzy's, and among them are the following: the Ottawa International Jazz Festival, Ronnie Scott's in London, the S.S. Oosterdam jazz cruise, the Tel Aviv Jazz Festival, and multiple others. The Joy Of Jazz event in Johannesburg, South Africa, featured three internationally known Steinway pianists, including Abdullah Ibraham and Ahmad Jamal. She was one of them.
